title: Friday Sermon 59 by Dean Mahmoud: Adam and Eve's Garments, Bodies, and Temptation (1982-11-19)
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/59 - Friday Sermon 19 Nov 1982 By Dean Mahmoud.csv
document_summary: Dean Mahmoud delivers a sermon continuing an earlier discussion of Adam and Eve. He argues that the original garments in the garden may represent natural obedience, that Satan stripped these garments by producing disobedience, and that the later garment of righteousness belongs to Adam's descendants. He carefully distinguishes factual nakedness from interpretive language about shameful parts and warns against importing biblical moral vocabulary into the Quran. A detailed Arabic comparison of Quran 7:20 and 20:120 examines angels, immortality, the tree of eternity, and everlasting kingship. Dean concludes that Adam and Eve were mortal earthly beings who failed an intended period of training and discovered their limited bodies after the temptation.

sections.title: Review of the garden, hunger and nakedness, garments of obedience, and the garment of righteousness
sections.summary: Dean reviews Quran 20:118 and 7:22–27. Adam and Eve did not hunger or go naked in the garden. Their original covering may symbolize natural obedience, Satan's temptation stripped that obedience, and later scripture promises Adam's descendants a better garment of righteousness.
related_questions: What did the original garment symbolize?
How did the garment of righteousness differ?

sections.title: Bodies, nakedness, shame, translation methodology, and biblical influence
sections.summary: Dean compares translations of Quran 7:27 that say bodies, nakedness, shame, or shameful parts. He distinguishes factual description from moral evaluation and suspects that some shame language entered through influence from the Hebrew Bible.
related_questions: What methodological distinction did Dean make?
Why did he prefer body or nakedness over shameful parts?
sections.retrieval_note: The biblical-influence claim requires textual-historical review.
sections.canonical_text: This is now, we're becoming very, very curious. In Sura 7, verse 27, Allah said, that Satan removes their garments, in order to show them their bodies. That's very interesting, you know. This is Ustaz's (teacher) translation "bodies." Other translators said "shame", "nakedness." And another translator said, "to show them their shameful parts." This is more explicit. Okay. Now, let's go to a problem of methodology. Here, we have, I believe, allegories or Masalan (مَثَلًۭا) involved. It's not, not something explicit like Wudu (Ablution). When Allah said, [5:6] ... (1) wash your faces, ... That's clear. [5:6] ... (1) wash your faces, ... However, you do it, [5:6] ... (1) wash your faces, ... Wash your hands, up to the elbows. Those are very clear. And Allah says so. There are verses that are clear. But, Masalans (مَثَلًۭا), allegories, are for people to reflect upon, to try to get messages, to draw implications, to draw ramifications. And, as long as we do not use these Masalans (مَثَلًۭا) to cast diversion of the memory of Allah, or as long as we don't use these Masalans (مَثَلًۭا) to cause division among the (unintelligible) of the believers, which Allah wants us, there are people who use these allegories to cast division. As long as we use them to understand more the Quran, to increase our Iman (faith), or to develop our understanding, I think we should not be afraid to try to get into the meaning, because as I said before, Allah presents these Masalans (مَثَلًۭا), these allegories, for men to reflect upon. And I hope I'm doing this for better understanding. The Quran is rich, so rich you can keep on getting more and more out of it. It's like a good orange. You keep on squeezing and squeezing, you can get as much orange juice as you want, make marmalade out of it, and make glazed candies out of it, (unintelligible) orange remains as is. This is, I think, a miracle of the Quran. I don't know why I'm talking of food so early in the morning. Now, the question again. What was disclosed? The crucial word here is Saw'atun (سَوْءَٰتِ) (unintelligible) Saw'at (سَوْءَٰتِ) This has been interpreted by some people within the Arabic context, not just when they translate in English. "Ashamed" "Secret parts" "Hidden parts" "bodies" and so on. A very primitive meaning is that it refers to something that is covered. Okay, please, let's put our attention to that. It means something that is covered, something that is not shown, something that you are unaware of, unconscious of. Now, take this word, "bodies." Translation of Ustaz (teacher). This to me, or what one is unaware of, is factual. All the (unintelligible), correct? To say that a body is exposed, it's factual, only attempts to be factual. But if you say, "shameful parts", if you say "shame", then you are now interpreting, right? You are putting a moral value. To say someone is naked, that's a fact. But to say that someone is showing his or her shameful parts, that is more than the fact. That is something that involves a fact coupled with a valid judgment. You see, the person is naked, and it's not good. These are two different... Now, let's make that distinction. Those who say, "shameful parts", "shame", are now putting a value judgment. And I suspect, this comes because of influence of reading the Jewish Bible. And I'm glad, Ustaz (teacher) just says that. He didn't say a shameful body. Indeed, I'll go further and say, what is covered? What is hidden? What one is unaware of is not necessarily something that is shameful. It only means it's something one is not conscious about. And thus, my method in this Khutba today is to try to accommodate, more or less within a general feeling, this possible interpretation in a manner that would be intelligible, in a manner that would give credit to each and every one of these interpreters and so on. IN SHAA ALLAH. But first, we must study a little closer the nature of the temptation caused by Satan. The temptation which brought about the disrobing of Adam and Eve. There are two forms of the statement of temptation.

sections.title: Mortality, failed training, earthly bodies, and the discovery of human limitation
sections.summary: Dean argues that Adam and Eve were always intended to be mortal beings of Earth and that Satan deceived them because neither immortality nor angelhood followed. He compares their expulsion with students failing an early term of training and says they then recognized bodies limited by space, time, flesh, blood, and mortality.
related_questions: What did Adam and Eve fail to become?
How did the school analogy explain expulsion?
What did they discover about their bodies?
sections.canonical_text: The plan was, from the beginning, they were mortals made of earth, they will be sent to earth, and they will have to die on earth. Or nothing for Satan. You, you cannot tempt them with immortality and so on. That's the first thing. The second one, old men say that deceived Adam and Eve. Why? Because after they ate of the tree, they did not become immortal, they did not become angels, right? It's very important. And not only that, they still had to go to earth, according to the original plan, as (unintelligible) Number three, Adam and Eve had, on account of this temptation, they were aspiring for something that they were not, and for which, I'm now submitting this, they were not ready before. In other words, they were not ready, they did not have the equipment, or the instruction, of how to become angels, or how to become immortal. The fourth one is that death, is not a punishment for the disobedience. No. Because they were destined to die from the beginning, right? So, dying is not a punishment for disobedience, for from the very beginning, they were mortal. And the fifth is that, what really happened was that, they were, they were untimely evicted from the garden. It's just like, they were supposed to leave the garden, but in this case, they left a little bit early than that was planned, although Allah knows this will happen. It's like a student who goes to college, he's supposed to stay four years or six years in college, depending on the degree, but if he lacks the first semester, then he is, he's kicked out. But this is what happened to our great grandparents. They were supposed to stay there for some time, I suppose, being taught more and trained, but they were kicked out a little bit, or very much earlier. They flunked, in other words. They were supposed to stay there temporarily, but not, although they were meant to stay there temporarily, the idea was not to have them kicked out, like a first-semester student who flunked. They were supposed to have to stay longer. Anyhow. When, when Adam and Eve did not get what they aspired to, when they did not become what they hoped for or wanted, they must have found out what they really were. And this is that they had bodies of flesh and blood, of earth, bodies limited by space-time coordinates, by space-time limitations. They realized that their bodies were of mortal stuff. See, they did not become immortal or angels. Then, they realized that their bodies were limited. They knew that they were mortal. Scales fell from their eyes. They realized that they were made out of bodies. And that, I think, I accept, (unintelligible) they were aware of their bodies, bodies that were supposed to rot, bodies that has blood. They realized they were deceived by Satan. They realized that they were vulnerable. They were in a precautious, precarious condition. They felt helpless. And more than ever, they needed Allah, alright? Aware of their bodies does not mean ashamed of their bodies. This is what I'm trying to say. Awareness of their bodies means that their bodies was, were limited. Neither this nor that were immortal. It was going to decay, and so on. Now to accommodate the thinking of the other students of the Quran, I submit that if there was any shame at all, it was not so much shame of the bodies, but it was the shame for disobeying Allah, alright? Allah had given them so much. Allah had given them food. Allah had given them clothing. Allah had warned them about Satan. They were not equal to the occasion. What existed now in their lives was a disharmony, a disequilibrium. Things were not what they were supposed to be. Things were not given them joy. It was, let's say, a world of square pegs and round holes all over. A disequilibrium. It was an atmosphere of living in a form of justice, brought by themselves to themselves. Things were not in their proper places. And as you all know, justice, one of the meanings of justice is putting things on the right position, giving things their proper joy. And they were helpless, abandoned by their sincere advisor, at least that's what Satan claimed he was. Later, there was no one to turn to, except Allah. This was a demo... (unintelligible) This is a dramatic recognition of Allah as the Lord. Dean Mahmoud: And this ...
